Follow-up 1: yes - the rewrite keeps the rotation identity in the metadata line, so the archived head stays reachable.

Follow-up 4, in full. The short answer above holds. This is the walk-through behind it.

## What the metadata line carries

The first line of the live file is metadata, not a message. After a rewrite it keeps the fields that tie the live file to its archive segment.

| Field | What it records | Kept by a rewrite |
| --- | --- | --- |
| rotation_generation | How many times the file has rotated | Yes |
| rotated_at | When the last rotation happened | Yes |
| title | The name shown in the session list | Yes |
| pinned | Whether the session restores as a slot | Yes |

Because the rotation fields survive, the reader still finds the archived head and still treats it as the start of the corpus.

## How the two files line up

The full corpus is the archived rows followed by the live rows, so a row index means the same thing before and after a rewrite.

1. The archive segment holds the 60 oldest rows.
2. The live file holds every row after them.
3. The first page returns the live rows, with has_more true.
4. next_before is 60, the count of archived rows.
5. A request with before=60 returns rows out of the archive.

## Checks to run after a rewrite

```text
archive rows    60, in the same order as before
live rows       same order and count as before
next_before     equals the archived row count
has_more        true while an archive segment exists
```

If any line stops holding, the join between the two files has moved.

## Things that do not change the answer

- Streamed chunks fold into one row before they are counted, so next_before counts messages and not deltas.
- A session that never rotated has no segment, so has_more stays false and there is nothing to page.
- Pinning only decides whether the session restores as a slot. It has no effect on paging.
- The title is cosmetic and plays no part in locating the archive.

## Walking it by hand

1. Open the pinned session from the Sessions rail.
2. Scroll to the top of the transcript.
3. Use the control for loading earlier messages.
4. Confirm older rows appear above the ones already shown.
5. Repeat until the control goes away.

## What to watch on screen

This reply is long on purpose. Scroll down through it and the prompt that started the turn should stay in the banner at the top of the transcript, because no later prompt has arrived to replace it.

Keep going to the end of this message and the banner should still show Follow-up 4. Scroll back up and the banner hands over to the transcript row once the prompt is on screen again.

## Summary

The live tail lines up with the archived head after a rewrite as long as the metadata line keeps its rotation identity. The cursor then counts the same rows as before, and every page is a plain slice of one ordered list.
